USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Iron amplifies oxidative injury

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

In an experimental cell suspension, hydrogen peroxide alone causes modest membrane damage. Adding unbound ferrous iron markedly increases damage, while an iron chelator reduces it. Generation of which species best explains the additional injury?

  1. Hydroxyl radical
  2. Molecular nitrogen
  3. Bicarbonate alone
  4. Glutathione disulfide
  5. Superoxide dismutase
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Hydroxyl radical

Redox-active ferrous iron reacts with peroxide in Fenton chemistry, generating highly reactive hydroxyl radicals near cellular targets.

Understanding the options

Hydroxyl radical
Redox-active ferrous iron reacts with peroxide in Fenton chemistry, generating highly reactive hydroxyl radicals near cellular targets.
Molecular nitrogen
Nitrogen does not mediate the iron-peroxide reaction.
Bicarbonate alone
Bicarbonate is not the highly reactive product asked about.
Glutathione disulfide
Oxidized glutathione indicates antioxidant consumption but is not the primary Fenton radical.
Superoxide dismutase
This is an enzyme rather than a reactive species.
